name: How to Level and Compare Commercial Construction Bids in Los Angeles County

mainEntity.name: How can a commercial owner in Los Angeles County compare bids fairly when contractors use different allowances, exclusions, and contingency assumptions?
mainEntity.text: How can a commercial owner in Los Angeles County compare bids fairly when contractors use different allowances, exclusions, and contingency assumptions?

acceptedAnswer.text: Commercial bid comparisons in Los Angeles County can be misleading if owners focus only on total price without examining how each contractor defines scope, allowances, and contingencies. Contractors may include different material quality levels, assume varying extents of unforeseen work, or exclude items like permits, utility fees, or specialty systems. To compare bids fairly, owners should create a bid-leveling matrix listing key scope items—such as structural systems, façade types, MEP systems, finishes, site work, and allowances—and capturing how each contractor has priced or excluded them. Items shown as exclusions or qualifications in one bid but included in another should be normalized by adding or subtracting costs to align assumptions. Differences in contingency, general conditions, and fee percentages should also be noted. In some cases, a higher base price with more realistic contingencies and fewer exclusions may represent a lower risk choice than a cheaper bid that will likely generate change orders. Discussing bids with each contractor and asking them to clarify or reprice specific items based on a standard scope description further improves comparability. Engaging the design team or an independent cost consultant to review bids can help identify gaps and ensure that the selected contractor can deliver the desired project at the agreed price.
acceptedAnswer.description: Fair bid comparison in Los Angeles County requires normalizing contractor proposals by aligning allowances, clarifying exclusions, and adjusting for differing contingency assumptions. Owners should create a bid-leveling matrix to see true price differences and ensure scope coverage before selecting a contractor based solely on headline numbers.
